attributes.provenance: Found by the build, not by reasoning: the first composed rule for G3DReadControlPadStates failed with `+0x18: relocated word inside the proof span` the moment it ran through apply_patch, on a span that contained no relocated word before the permutation. Landed 2026-09-01 in worktree GDL-Claude-G3dClose, commit 7697345aa. tools/gdl/webfrank.py: _IMMEDIATE_ONLY_RELOCATIONS, the restructured relocation handling in prove_constant_source, relocation_types plumbed through equivalent_copy_form, and the apply_patch re-derivation. tools/gdl/tests/test_webfrank.py: 4 new cases in RelocatedWordInsideProofSpanTests (104 -> 108).

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
COMPOSING WEBFRANK STAGES BREAKS AN ASSUMPTION EVERY SINGLE-STAGE RULE COULD SAFELY MAKE: that the relocation table captured at the top of apply_patch still describes the object the LATER stages see. It does not. instruction_permutation rewrites the relocation records, so a word that carried no relocation can acquire one and vice versa, and every later stage consumes relocated_offsets as a FAIL-CLOSED input. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS FOLLOWED, both now fixed, and both invisible to any rule that uses only one stage - which is why no previous rule tripped them.

DEFECT 1, STALENESS. apply_patch computed relocated_offsets and call_targets ONCE, before the permutation, and passed those stale sets to equivalent_copy_form. On G3DReadControlPadStates the ADDR16_LO half of gPadManager rides an atom from +0x14 to +0x18, so the stale set named the wrong instruction as relocated. It happened to be harmless here (the moved word writes r31, not the proof's source r29) but it is harmless BY LUCK, and a fail-closed guard fed a stale input is not fail-closed. apply_patch now re-derives relocated_offsets, call_targets and relocation_types from the PATCHED object immediately after the permutation. A scratch harness that modelled the relocation move by hand got this wrong in the opposite direction and reported a false PASS; the real build, with the fix, refused correctly. RECORDED AS A METHOD LESSON: prove composed stages through apply_patch against the real object, never through a hand-rolled replay of what you believe the earlier stage did - the harness and the guard disagreed, and the guard was right.

DEFECT 2, OVER-BROAD REFUSAL, and the subtlety that makes it a real check rather than a formality. prove_constant_source refused ANY relocated word anywhere in the span. The rationale is sound but applies only to the DEFINITION: an unresolved address half is not the literal the proof needs. An INTERPOSED relocated word that does not write the source register cannot change the source - but that reasoning depends on the decoded write set, and a write set is decoded from opcode and register fields. So it is trustworthy only if the relocation cannot rewrite those bits. R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 is the counterexample: it rewrites the base REGISTER field to r2/r13. The refusal is therefore now type-checked, not dropped: _IMMEDIATE_ONLY_RELOCATIONS = {3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 11} (ADDR16, ADDR16_LO, ADDR16_HI, ADDR16_HA, REL24, REL14), deliberately EXCLUDING whole-word ADDR32/REL32 and SDA21, and the type is validated BEFORE the word is decoded. A relocated word that IS the definition is still refused unconditionally, whatever its type. An unknown or absent type fails closed.

GENERAL RULE FOR THE NEXT COMPOSED LANE: any stage that consumes relocation state must consume it as re-derived after every preceding stage, and any guard that reasons from decoded instruction fields must first establish that no relocation on that word can rewrite those fields. Both obligations are invisible until stages are composed, so expect to meet them for the first time on your first multi-stage rule.
